text:
maria: heads up — saw a provisioning wave this morning where ~8 GPU pods stayed Pending. root cause looks like node scratch IO going into prolonged iowait and the kubelet marking nodes NotReady for scheduling. collecting logs now.

maria: dmesg snippet from one node:
```
[  120.123456] nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 11 timeout, reset controller
[  120.456789] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2345678
[  121.000001] audit: type=1400 audit(1610000000.000:123): apparmor="DENIED" operation="open"...
```

tom: saw that too. autoscaler attempted to provision 5 preemptibles in us-west2 and they never passed Ready. node iowait jumped to ~70% for minutes. pods stayed Pending due to attach/detach timeouts.

anika: are we correlated to the nightly scrubs? I remember we rolled a more aggressive scrub sampler last week that increases concurrency.

ryan: confirmed — fstrim/scrub tasks were running on those hosts. `systemctl status scratch-scrub.timer` shows runs at 03:02 and several instances overlapped. one host had a stuck `fstrim -v /scratch` process.

jess: mitigation proposal: temporarily set scrub to passive on the candidate pool and scale up dedicated-gpu nodes for the critical queues. also throttle scrub concurrency in the scrubber config (reduce worker_count).

ops-oncall: +1. I patched the node affinity for the preemptible pool to exclude those nodes and kicked a clusterdrain for 6 nodes. also posted a quick runbook step: `systemctl stop scratch-scrub@{1..N}` and `echo 2 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio` to reduce writeback pressure while we stabilize. use with caution.

maria: thanks. I uploaded full logs and a heap of `iostat -x 1 10` captures to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1234 — summary: sustained write latency spikes + retry storms from nvme causing attach/detach retries and kubelet churn.

sre-bot: incident created: INF-1234 — local-disk-io-quiver. Severity: P2. Assigned to ops-oncall, due in 2h. :rotating_light:

ryan: short-term actions I ran: 1) disabled scrub concurrency on candidate pool 2) cordoned/evicted pods from the worst 6 nodes 3) temporarily bumped autoscaler headroom by 10% so the control plane doesn't keep trying to place on degraded nodes. so far new nodes are Healthy.

jess: long-term: add an autoscaler predicate for node iowait/ioutil and add a pre-provision probe that runs `fio --rw=readwrite --iodepth=4 --runtime=5` against /scratch before handing node to kubelet. also document acceptable iowait thresholds.

anika: also let's add a nightly soft-stop window for scrubs in high-util regions (us-west2) during the 02:00-05:00 provisioning window. and we should re-evaluate scrub sampling to avoid hotspots.

maria: agreed. created follow-ups in INF-1234: (a) short-term scrub throttling automation (b) autoscaler predicate + metrics (c) probe job + policy. ops-oncall — can you keep the candidate pool restricted for 1 hour and then revert if stable?

ops-oncall: done, will monitor for 45m and post updates.

jess: one more low-risk tweak: for any node with >40% iowait we should set `kubelet.evictionThresholds.disk` more conservatively so we stop scheduling before pod attach storms.

maria: good call. will add to INF-1234. thanks everyone — rolling postmortem/notes to #postmortems after we close the ticket. :slightly_smiling_face:
